countries.name: Brazil
countries.what: The last polls before the runoff, released Oct 24, lean slightly to Flavio Bolsonaro: Datafolha 51% to 49% (from 50% to 50% on Oct 22), Quaest 51% to 49% and AtlasIntel 50.8% to 49.2% of valid votes, all inside their margins of error. Betting markets put him near 80%.
countries.for_you: No trades before Monday's open settles. If Lula wins and NU falls into its 14.13 to 15.02 zone, wait for a day when buyers lead before a small first buy; if Flavio wins and NU opens above about 15.32, do not chase. The tickers are left out of both lists because the result is not known.

countries.name: Gulf (Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Iran risk)
countries.what: On Oct 24 the Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on an Aramco site at Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery, crude pumping stations and the East-West pipeline, the route Saudi Arabia uses to ship around Hormuz. The coalition said it shot down two missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif, and no damage was confirmed by early Sunday. Yanbu hosts SAMREF, a 50/50 refinery of Aramco and ExxonMobil.
countries.for_you: If you hold energy swings, keep the stops (XOM 162.99, CVX 210.45) and do not add on a Monday oil gap; both report Oct 30. SLB is left out of both lists: higher prices help, but strikes on Saudi sites put its largest region at risk.
